text.guided:
Every point of the plane is built from two arrows: î = (1, 0) goes one step right, ĵ = (0, 1) goes one step up. Move those two arrows and the whole grid follows them, like a net pulled by two corners.

The matrix is just the list of where the arrows land: **column 1 = where î lands, column 2 = where ĵ lands**.
text.fast: A 2×2 matrix is two columns: column 1 is the image of î = (1, 0), column 2 is the image of ĵ = (0, 1). Everything else follows by linearity.

examples.games: Think of a game camera: dragging two handles at the corners of the screen stretches or tilts everything you see.
examples.physics: Think of a rubber sheet pinned at the origin: pull the tip of each unit arrow and every drawn shape deforms with it.
examples.ai: Think of a layer that remaps two input features to new directions: the weights are exactly where each basis arrow ends up.

scene.caption: î moves to (2, 0): the whole grid stretches to the right
ĵ moves to (1, 1): the grid leans

check.prompt: Make the plane twice as wide and keep its height: drag î and ĵ to the right spots.

text.guided:
A point like (2, 1) means "2 steps of î and 1 step of ĵ". When the arrows move, the point keeps its recipe: it lands on 2 × (new î) + 1 × (new ĵ).

So to follow any point, only ever track the two arrows.
text.fast: $M\,(x, y) = x\cdot M\hat\imath + y\cdot M\hat\jmath$. Track the columns, then recombine.

examples.games: A character stuck to a sticker on the screen moves with the sticker: same recipe, new axes.
examples.physics: A mark painted on the stretched sheet stays at the same grid coordinates, whatever the sheet does.
examples.ai: An input (x, y) is a weighted sum of the two basis directions; the layer just reweights them.

check.prompt: A matrix sends î to (1, 0) and ĵ to (1, 1). Place the point where (2, 1) lands.

text.guided: Swapping the two columns gives a different transformation: the first column always belongs to î, the second to ĵ. Mix them up and your shape ends up mirrored across the diagonal.
text.fast: Column 1 = image of î, column 2 = image of ĵ. Swapping columns reflects the plane across y = x.

examples.games: Controls swapped: pressing right now moves you up, and up moves you right.
examples.physics: Exchanging the x and y axes of a lab frame mirrors every measurement across the diagonal.
examples.ai: Feeding features in the wrong order silently swaps what each weight means.

check.prompt: Which matrix swaps î and ĵ (î lands on (0, 1) and ĵ lands on (1, 0))?
